HomePage.Overview of Cashu and its Concepts: Overview of Cashu and its Concepts
HomePage.title: classu.cash
HomePage.subtitle: Cashu is privacy-preserving digital cash using blind signatures
HomePage.Bob signs tokens: Bob signs tokens without seeing their content, ensuring privacy. The token is a combination of Alice's secret + Bob's signature. When Carol redeems it, Bob can verify it's valid but can't link it back to Alice.
HomePage.PRIVACY: Bob: PRIVACY: Bob doesn't know Carol's token came from Alice!
HomePage.ph1 description: Alice creates a secret message and gets Bob (the mint operator) to blindly sign it
HomePage.ph1 st3: Bob signs the blinded message (without seeing it)
HomePage.ph1 st4: Alice unblinds to get a valid token
HomePage.ph2 description: Alice sends the token privately to Carol, off-chain
HomePage.ph2 st1: Alice sends the valid token to Carol
HomePage.ph2 st3: No blockchain needed - instant and private
HomePage.ph3 description: Carol redeems the token with Bob and receives funds
HomePage.ph3 st1: Carol sends the token back to Bob
HomePage.ph3 st2: Bob verifies the token hasn't been spent
HomePage.ph3 st3: Bob checks the spent secrets database
HomePage.ph3 st4: Carol receives funds, token is marked as spent
HomePage.ph3 st5: Bob doesn't know the token came from Alice (PRIVACY!)

nut00.subtitle: Notation, Utilization, and Terminology
nut00.This specification defines: This specification defines the core notation, cryptographic models, and terminology used throughout the Cashu protocol for privacy-preserving digital cash.
nut00.The protocol uses: The protocol uses Blind Diffie-Hellmann Key Exchange (BDHKE) to enable the mint to sign tokens without seeing their content. This ensures that when Carol redeems a token, Bob can verify its validity but cannot link it back to Alice.
nut00.Bob signs the token: Bob signs the token without ever seeing the secret x. When Carol redeems it, Bob can verify it's valid but cannot determine who originally created it.
nut00.Deterministically maps a: Deterministically maps a message to a curve point
nut00.Sent from Alice to: Sent from Alice to Bob for minting or swapping
nut00.Keyset ID from: Keyset ID from which to expect signature
nut00.Sent from Bob to Alice after signing: Sent from Bob to Alice after signing
nut00.Used by Alice to spend tokens: Used by Alice to spend tokens
nut00.For NFC transmission: For NFC transmission, tokens use a binary prefix
nut00.Part of the Cashu Protocol Specification: Part of the Cashu Protocol Specification
nut00.bdhkeSt_1_description: The mint publishes its public key K, derived from private key k and generator point G
nut00.bdhkeSt_2_description: Alice picks a secret x, hashes it to curve point Y, then blinds it with random factor r
nut00.bdhkeSt_3_description: Alice sends the blinded message B_ to Bob without revealing her secret
nut00.bdhkeSt_4_description: Bob signs the blinded message without seeing the actual secret
nut00.bdhkeSt_5_description: Bob sends back the blind signature to Alice
nut00.bdhkeSt_6_description: Alice removes the blinding factor to get the final signature C
nut00.bdhkeSt_7_description: Alice can now send the pair (secret, signature) as a token to Carol
nut00.bdhkeSt_8_description: Bob verifies the token is valid and marks the secret as spent
nut00.v_alice_r_desc: Random value to blind the secret

nut01.subtitle: Mint public key exchange
nut01.description_detail: Alice (wallet) receives Bob's (mint) public keys via GET /v1/keys to unblind blind signatures (NUT-00).
nut01.active_keysets_detail: The mint only responds with 'active' keysets, which are used for new signatures. Inactive keysets are accepted for inputs but not used for new outputs.
nut01.endpoint_detail: The primary endpoint for requesting the mint's active keysets.
nut01.response_detail: The response contains an array of active keysets.
nut01.currency_units_detail: Mints can support various units for minting (NUT-04) and melting (NUT-05).
nut01.minor_unit_rule_detail: For Bitcoin and ISO 4217 currencies, Keyset amount values MUST represent an amount in the Minor Unit of that currency (e.g., sat for btc, cent for usd).
nut01.keyset_generation_detail: Keysets are generated by the mint, identified by an 'id' computable from its public keys (NUT-02).
nut01.keys_map_detail: Keysets are maps of {<amount_i> : <mint_pubkey_i>}. The public key MUST use the compressed Secp256k1 format.

nut02.subtitle: Defines the properties of a Keyset, the endpoints to retrieve them, and how the Keyset ID is derived.
nut02.KeysetIDDesc: A keyset ID is an identifier that can be derived by anyone who knows the set of a mint's public keys. Wallets CAN compute the ID to verify the mint is supplying the correct ID.
nut02.ActiveKeysetsDesc1: Mints MUST have at least one 'active' keyset. This property determines if the mint allows new ecash to be generated from this keyset. Only new outputs MUST come from active keysets.
nut02.ActiveKeysetsDesc2: Wallets SHOULD prioritize 'swapping' Proofs from inactive keysets (see NUT-03) to quickly eliminate them.
nut02.FeesDesc: Keysets indicate the 'input_fee_ppk' fee charged when a Proof from that keyset is spent as an input in a transaction. The fee is given in parts per thousand (ppk) per input.
nut02.TxConstructionDesc: When constructing a transaction, wallets MUST add fees to the inputs or, conversely, subtract them from the outputs. The total fee is the sum of the fees of each input, rounded up to the next integer.
nut02.DerivingIDDesc: The ID is a lowercase hexadecimal string, prefixed with a version byte ('00'). It is derived by sorting public keys by amount, concatenating them, performing SHA256 HASH, and taking the first 14 characters of the hex hash, prefixed with '00'.
nut02.GetKeysetsEndpointDesc: A wallet can ask the mint for a list of all keysets (active and inactive) via this endpoint.
nut02.GetKeysEndpointDesc: To receive the public keys for a specific keyset, a wallet can call this endpoint.
nut02.FeeExampleDetail: Example: A 100 ppk fee means 0.1 sat per input. The total fee is rounded up to the next integer. Spending 3 inputs: 300 ppk total. Rounded up = 1 sat.
nut02.ResponseDetailKeysets: The response contains a list of keysets, with their ID, unit, 'active' status, and 'input_fee_ppk'.
nut02.ImplementationFlow_1: If we do not yet have keys from this mint, get all keys: GET /v1/keys and store them.
nut02.ImplementationFlow_3: For all new keysets returned that we do not yet have, fetch them using GET /v1/keys/{keyset_id} and store them.
nut02.ImplementationFlow_4: If any of the keysets have changed their 'active' flag, update it in the db and use the keyset accordingly.
nut02.description_detail: A keyset is a set of public keys, each corresponding to a supported amount (e.g., 1, 2, 4, 8...). It includes an ID, a currency unit, an active flag, and an input fee.
nut02.id_detail_1: A unique identifier for a keyset, derived deterministically from its public keys. Wallets can compute this ID to verify the mint's response.
nut02.id_detail_2: The ID is used in Proofs, BlindedMessages, and BlindSignatures to link them to a specific set of keys.
nut02.active_detail_1: Keysets marked as 'active' are used by the mint to sign new outputs. The mint MUST have at least one active keyset.
nut02.active_detail_2: Inactive keysets are accepted for inputs (to be spent) but not used for new outputs.
nut02.fees_detail: The 'input_fee_ppk' determines the fees for spending ecash from this keyset.
nut02.get_all_active_detail: Returns only the active keysets (used for new signatures).
nut02.get_all_all_detail: Returns a list of all keysets, both active and inactive.
nut02.get_single_by_id_detail: Returns a specific keyset by its ID, whether it is active or inactive.
nut02.algorithm_desc: The Keyset ID is derived from the list of public keys (K) within that set to ensure consistent identification.
nut02.step_1_detail: Gather all public keys (K) in compressed Secp256k1 format (33 bytes).
nut02.step_2_detail: Sort the public keys based on their corresponding amount values in ascending order (e.g., 1, 2, 4, 8...).
nut02.step_3_detail: Concatenate the sorted public keys into a single binary string in the order of their amounts.
nut02.step_4_detail: Calculate the SHA256 hash of the resulting concatenated string.
nut02.step_5_detail: Truncate the SHA256 hash to its first 8 bytes and encode the result as a hexadecimal string. This is the Keyset ID.
nut02.wallet_note_2: Wallets SHOULD request all keysets via `GET /v1/keysets` to get all properties, including fees, for a new mint.
nut02.wallet_note_3: Wallets MUST respect the `active` and `input_fee_ppk` properties.

nut03.subtitle: The swap operation is the most important component of the Cashu system. A swap operation consists of multiple inputs (Proofs) and outputs (BlindedMessages). Mints verify and invalidate the inputs and issue new promises (BlindSignatures).
nut03.SwapDesc: The swap operation serves multiple use cases: splitting tokens to target amounts or receiving tokens from another user.
nut03.SendTitle: Swap to Send: Alice wants to send 40 sat
nut03.SendExampleDetail: Alice has [32, 16, 16] sat (total 64). She requests outputs [8, 32, 8, 16] sat (total 64). The first two tokens can now be combined for 40 sat. The original inputs are invalidated.
nut03.PrivacyNoteDesc: To preserve privacy, wallets SHOULD ensure the requested output list is sorted by amount in ascending order. This mitigates information leakage to the mint regarding the exact amount being prepared for payment.
nut03.ReceiveDesc: Carol can receive Alice's tokens using the same swap operation. Carol uses Alice's tokens as inputs (to invalidate them) and requests new outputs from Bob. Only after Carol has redeemed the new outputs, Alice can no longer double-spend.
nut03.EndpointDesc: The endpoint for swapping tokens. It consists of multiple inputs (Proofs) and outputs (BlindedMessages).
nut03.RequestDetail: The 'inputs' array contains the existing tokens to invalidate. The 'outputs' array contains the BlindedMessages for the new tokens to be signed.
nut03.ResponseDetail: The response contains an array of BlindSignatures (promises for new tokens).
